lead: you wrote to a man you had met once, eleven years on, and opened with the thing he said about his brother. he had to be told twice who you were.
sun: resuming wants a first time to resume, and yours are unusually small — twenty minutes on a platform, one shift, an afternoon in a house you were in by mistake. any of them is enough to lower something into. the people you go and retrieve spoke to you once, and what turns up at their door years later is somebody arriving mid-sentence, warm, with the whole of that afternoon still live.
moon: the reading was finished inside the first minute and has not thinned since — how he stood, the pause in front of his brother's name, which of the two he was protecting. that is what makes a second approach possible: there is something at full size to reach for. he holds nothing of you at that grain. what you are resuming, he is being introduced to.
pull: every friendship you have dates from a minute the other person cannot place. you kept it whole, you came for it, and they are handed their own sentence by a stranger.
tension: he placed you eventually, and then the accuracy did the damage. nobody carries that much of one afternoon unless something was going on, and the word people reach for is intense, or lonely, and neither is arguable from where he stands. the answer to it — that twenty minutes registered at a resolution he has no experience of — plays worse than the charge. so the warmth arrives as a claim on him, and he answers it carefully.
cost: twenty minutes is enough to build a decade on here, and none of it is technique — the thread stayed live throughout, so nothing needs re-establishing at either end. the same fidelity has no off position. everybody you have stood next to went in at full strength, and the ones you never went and got are in there too, held by one party with no plans for them.

lead: you have left the place twice and been readmitted twice, at grade, and on neither morning did anybody ask where you had been or what you imagined you were owed.
sun: leaving here was never resignation on your own account. the post was set down rather than surrendered, and a thing set down is temporary, so nothing was done that would need undoing. what gets you in again is not an application. you walk the same corridor on an ordinary wednesday and resume the file at the paragraph it stopped at, and an institution with no procedure for that finds accommodating you cheaper than querying it.
moon: none of it can be seen to be wanted. re-entry at that bearing does not look like re-entry — it reads as a recall arranged above, by people the room assumes it was not told about. nobody has asked you to account for the years out, and nobody has said out loud that the place kept the seat open, which would settle what you are worth to it.
pull: twice out, twice in, and nobody in that building ever had to decide whether to have you. the chair was warm both times, and why it was warm has never been put to you.
tension: entitled has never been said about you, and the ones who never left have the most cause to say it. two departures, two restorations, no fee visible on either — the manner you came in by gives them nothing to lodge against. what circulates instead is that you are the sort of person a place makes room for. close enough to true to be unanswerable, and it works inside, where making room for you is not choosing you.
cost: you can pick a position up at the level you set it down, inside a fortnight, with everything you knew about the building intact, which the people who stayed could not do and have never had cause to learn. every year of standing you hold there is a year somebody elected not to fill the seat. the test takes staying, and staying is what your record cannot show.

lead: the leaving drew a bigger crowd than the work ever did, and inside two years you were doing it again, to that crowd. neither ending was theatre, and neither was taken at its word.
sun: nothing you resume gets resumed quietly. the old material, the lapsed friendship, the practice you let go of at twenty-six — all of it goes up where the room can watch it going up, since there is no other setting available to do it at. and the room prefers the resumption to the work. a first attempt has to be judged on what it is. a second one only has to arrive.
moon: being looked at was never the difficulty, so nothing in you shrinks at a reappearance, and the reappearance is wider than whatever you brought with you. at that width a return lands as an occasion whether or not what came again is any good, since the room is answering the fact of it. every second attempt of your life has been received before anything in it was heard.
pull: no second attempt of yours has ever had to be good. the room is glad before it hears anything, and nothing you have taken up again has come home with a verdict on it.
tension: unkillable is the word, said fondly, by people who have watched three restarts from the same seats. it also fixes the terms. an ending announced by you gets received as the opening half of something, so on the two occasions you meant it the room waited, warmly, for years, and called the waiting loyalty. nothing you say in public gets taken as final, and a thing this well lit is assumed to be on its way in.
cost: an audience that would make anybody else earn a hearing arrives at your second attempt already glad, so a thing shelved for years takes a fortnight to put up rather than a season. being done with something where nobody is watching is the one motion unavailable. every departure of yours enters somebody's calendar as an interval, and no room you left has had to sit with an ending.

lead: six years of silence ended because you rang, and the evening was warm and easy and completely genuine. whoever it was that loved her closed over in one season, and none of that has ever reached the table.
sun: you do not accept that a thing is gone. the number still works, the thread is still open, four silent years file as an interval rather than a verdict — so you draw it up, and it comes up in the condition it went down in, which is what keeps proving you right. every arrangement you let lapse is retrievable, and your record is long enough to make that a fact rather than a hope.
moon: underneath, nothing finishes by degrees. the season that held her turned over completely, in weeks, and whoever was her friend did not thin out — that person ended. what survives a turn like that is never the thing. it is her, and what is owed her. so the retrieval is real, carried out by somebody with no stake in the evening who would not dream of missing the date.
pull: everything you set down is still there, and you go for it. the one who wanted it finished in a season and left the debt behind, and the debt is what walks in the door.
tension: no version of the true account can be handed over. the only words for it — that you were finished with her long ago and would not consider not turning up — arrive as cruelty in the costume of honesty. so three of these evenings, spread across a decade, have each landed as devotion, and she describes the friendship as the one that never went anywhere, with the facts exactly right and every reason behind them wrong.
cost: people who assumed they were dropped learn otherwise, years later, and nothing in your life goes under for want of somebody prepared to reopen it — rare enough that they feel picked out. what they get is the whole resumption and none of the season it belonged to. and there is no telling which of them you would choose now, since choosing went with the one who did it.
